# A08 report: Campaign autopilot, pipeline, digest and notifications

Branch `v2-a08-campaign`. Everything lives in `server/campaign/**` and `server/notify/**`. Outside them, A08 rewrote `server/services/hunt.ts` as a compatibility shim and added `scripts/checks/a08-campaign.ts`. The lead baselines `pipeline.ts` and `claims.ts` were only extended: `transition()`, `ensurePipeline()`, `pipelineState()`, `claimJob()`, `releaseClaim()` and `activeClaim()` are unchanged.

## What was built

| File | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `campaign/campaigns.ts` | Campaign CRUD with validation (dates, pacing, time zone), status changes (draft → active ⇄ paused → ended), each emitting `campaign.status`, plus lifecycle metadata: first activation, when dry run went live, rehearse-only, status reason, final digest. Dry-run maths (`isDryRun`, `campaignDayIndex`, `liveAt`) counts in the campaign's local days. |
| `campaign/engine.ts` | The autopilot `Engine`. Each `tick()` checks the STOP file, the kill flag and the monthly AI budget. It ends campaigns at `endsAt`, pauses one when its own budget runs out, switches dry run to live, starts due background tasks (single-flight, cadence persisted across restarts), keeps the PC awake and hands the next job to the single apply worker. Also handles kill, recovery, digests and the owner's actions (start, pause, resume, end, run now, soft stop). |
| `campaign/worker.ts` | One job end to end: claim → write → route (email or form) → fill → verify → submit or rehearse → settle. Also does crash recovery (`recoverJob`). |
| `campaign/journal.ts` | The durable step journal (`campaign_steps`), saved packets (`campaign_packets`) and task bookkeeping (`campaign_tasks`). |
| `campaign/digest.ts` | Builds, renders (plain text, Telegram HTML, email HTML) and stores the daily and final digests. |
| `campaign/deps.ts` | The dependency seam. Production wires the real modules lazily; tests pass fakes. `NotImplemented` from any module means "stage unavailable": logged once, never fatal. |
| `campaign/kill.ts` | Persisted kill flag, `data/STOP` detection and `onKill()` hooks for anything holding a browser. |
| `campaign/awake.ts` | Windows keep-awake: a hidden PowerShell helper calling `SetThreadExecutionState(ES_CONTINUOUS \| ES_SYSTEM_REQUIRED)` while it blocks on stdin. Releasing it kills the helper, and if Bureau dies the pipe closes and the helper exits by itself. No-op on other platforms and in offline/selfcheck mode. `services/autostart.ts` is untouched. |
| `campaign/time.ts` | Intl-only time-zone arithmetic: active windows (overnight windows included), local days, ISO weeks, plus a location → time-zone table for employer business hours. |
| `campaign/clock.ts` | `Clock` seam, `FakeClock` with timers, and a seeded PRNG. |
| `campaign/settings.ts` | Global autopilot settings (global daily cap 25, profile sync 06:00, inbox every 5 min, weekly Monday 07:00, digest 15 min after hours close, keep-awake on, max 3 attempts, prefer employer hours) and the backoff schedule. |
| `campaign/answers.ts` | Owner answers to unknown questions. Uses A03's `answerUnknown` when it exists, otherwise a local adapter (see requests §1). |
| `campaign/schema.ts` | A08's five additive tables (see requests §6). |
| `campaign/routes.ts` | The UI routes (listed below). |
| `campaign/index.ts` | Contract entry points (`startCampaign`, `pauseCampaign`, `resumeCampaign`, `endCampaign`, `killAll`, `tick`, `startAutopilot`), the engine singleton, and the Telegram command handlers. |
| `notify/index.ts` | `notify(kind, payload)` (contract) and `deliver()`, which fans out to Telegram, ntfy and email, never throws, and reports which channels took it. |
| `notify/telegram.ts` | Bot API client (sendMessage, long-polled getUpdates, getMe) on undici to the fixed host `api.telegram.org`. HTTP layer is swappable. Refuses the network in offline/replay mode. Message chunking and HTML escaping. The token never appears in errors. |
| `notify/commands.ts` | Command parsing, the chat-id lock, and the long-poll loop (offset persisted before handling, so a crash never replays `/stop`). |
| `notify/questions.ts` | Pushes unknown questions to Telegram once each, with a 6-character short id, and maps reply messages back to questions. |
| `notify/email.ts`, `notify/ntfy.ts` | Digest by email over the existing SMTP account (to the owner only) and the ntfy channel (https only, topic in the vault). |
| `notify/settings.ts` | Channel switches (settings) and secrets (vault: `telegram_bot_token`, `telegram_chat_id`, `ntfy_topic`). Exposes a public view that never contains a secret. |
| `services/hunt.ts` | The `/api/hunt` shim, described below. |

### How a job moves (always through `transition()`)

`selected → writing → written → filling → verified → submitted | rehearsed`, with side exits: `skipped` (writer, uniqueness, form), `needs_you` (no route, truth lock not clean, could not verify, form asked, interrupted live submit) and `failed` (with backoff). Retries: `failed → written` when the packet is kept, or `→ selected`. At go-live: `rehearsed → written`. After an answer: `needs_you → written` or `skipped → selected`.

### Never submitting twice

1. Before any live form submit or email, a `submit_intent` row is committed. A result row (`outcome` or `submit_done`) is committed after.
2. On start, `recover()` releases the autopilot's own stale claims and settles every job it left in `writing`, `filling` or `verified`:
   - Writing with a saved packet goes to `written`. Without one it goes to `selected`.
   - A recorded "submitted" outcome, or an application row already `sent`, goes to `submitted`.
   - An open submit intent goes to `needs_you` with "check before applying again". The form is never re-opened.
   - A rehearsal that never reached submit goes back to `written` and is redone. A rehearsal can never submit.
3. Right before the irreversible step the worker re-checks: the job is not already `submitted`, there is no `sent` application row, the same canonical posting has not been submitted, and the company is not inside its cooldown. These checks run across all campaigns and include external submissions.
4. The claim (holder `autopilot`, renewed every 5 minutes) is held for the whole run. Jobs another holder claims are skipped.
5. The form engine's own guarantee (submit only when verified) is double-checked. A rehearsal outcome with `verified=false` goes to `needs_you`. If A05 ever reports `submitted` without verification, or during a rehearsal, A08 records it truthfully as submitted (so it is never retried), pauses the campaign and sends an alert.

### Pacing and caps

- One job at a time, globally.
- After real work the next job waits a random gap between `pacingMinutes.min` and `max`. After a skip the wait is 30 s; after an unavailable stage, 15 min.
- Jobs start only inside the campaign's `activeHours` (in its time zone).
- Among queued jobs, finished packets go first, then priority, then score. Jobs whose employer's zone is known but outside weekday 09:00–18:00 drop to the back of the queue.
- Caps: the campaign's `dailyCap` (live plus rehearsed, per campaign local day), the global cap (all campaigns, server local day), the campaign `budgetUsd` (pauses the campaign) and the monthly AI budget (trips the kill switch).
- Failures back off 30 min, 1 h, 2 h … up to 12 h, then the job stops after `maxAttempts`.

### Scheduler cadence

| Task | Cadence |
| --- | --- |
| Scout, then match, then select (per campaign) | Every `scoutEveryHours`, jittered 0–20% early (2.4–3 h at the default). Also immediately on start, resume and run-now. |
| Standalone match | Every 30 min, when jobs are pending. |
| Select | Every 5 min, topping the queue up to today's room. |
| Profile sync | Daily at 06:00 local. |
| Inbox poll | Every 5 min. |
| Gap report and company discovery | Weekly, Monday 07:00 local. |
| Recipe jobs | Every 6 h. |
| Unknown questions to Telegram | Every tick. |
| Daily digest | 15 min after the active window closes (23:30 for round-the-clock campaigns). |
| Kill-switch check (`data/STOP`) | Every 2 s. |

Ticks run every 15 s.

## Routes

| Method | Path | What |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/api/campaigns` | Every campaign with `meta` and `stats`, plus autopilot status |
| POST | `/api/campaigns` | Create (`{ name, config, start? }`) |
| GET | `/api/campaigns/defaults` | A starter config from the profile's preferences |
| GET | `/api/campaigns/status` | Kill state, STOP file, current job and step, next apply, keep-awake, tasks, global room |
| GET / PUT | `/api/campaigns/settings` | Global autopilot settings (PUT is partial) |
| POST | `/api/campaigns/run-now` | Scout now and skip the pacing wait once |
| GET | `/api/campaigns/jobs/:jobId/timeline` | Pipeline transitions and worker steps for one job, in time order |
| GET | `/api/campaigns/:id` | One campaign with `meta` and `stats` |
| PUT | `/api/campaigns/:id` | Rename and/or merge a partial config |
| DELETE | `/api/campaigns/:id` | Delete (409 while active) |
| POST | `/api/campaigns/:id/start` · `/pause` · `/resume` · `/end` | Lifecycle (`end` returns `finalDigestId`) |
| GET | `/api/campaigns/:id/pipeline` | Jobs in the campaign (`?state=a,b&limit=`) |
| GET | `/api/campaigns/:id/steps` | The worker journal (`?limit=`) |
| GET | `/api/digests` | Stored digests (`?campaignId=&limit=`) |
| GET | `/api/digests/:id` | One digest plus its plain-text rendering |
| POST | `/api/digests/preview` | Build today's digest without saving or sending (`{ campaignId? }`) |
| POST | `/api/digests/send` | Build, save and send now |
| GET | `/api/notify` | Channel switches and which secrets are set (never the secrets) |
| PUT | `/api/notify/settings` | Channel switches |
| PUT / DELETE | `/api/notify/telegram` | Save (`{ token?, chatId? }`) or forget the bot |
| GET | `/api/notify/telegram/chats` | Chats that recently messaged the bot (to find your chat id) |
| PUT | `/api/notify/ntfy` | ntfy topic (`{ topic \| null }`) |
| POST | `/api/notify/test` | Test message (`{ channel: telegram \| ntfy \| email }`) |
| GET / POST / DELETE | `/api/kill` | Read, trip (`{ reason? }`) and clear the kill switch |

The v1 routes `GET/PUT /api/hunt`, `POST /api/hunt/run` and `POST /api/hunt/stop` (in `routes/system.ts`, untouched) now go through `services/hunt.ts`:

- The hunt is "the active campaign" (else the shim's own campaign).
- Switching it on with no campaign creates an open-ended, round-the-clock "Hunt" campaign from the v1 settings and starts it. Off pauses it.
- `mode: rehearse` maps to rehearse-only.
- `run` triggers run-now. `stop` finishes the current application, then waits a full pacing gap.
- `huntStatus()` keeps its v1 shape and adds `campaign` and `kill`.
- `startHuntTimer()` is now a no-op: `startAutopilot()` drives everything.

## Telegram commands

`/status`, `/today`, `/pause <campaign>`, `/resume <campaign>` (name, id prefix, or nothing when only one fits), `/answer <id> <text>` (or just reply to the question message), `/stop` (the kill switch), `/help`. Only messages from the configured chat id are acted on. Messages from anyone else get no reply at all and are logged with a masked id.

## How to run and test

- `npm run selfcheck -- a08` runs 51 checks in about 13 s, all offline:
  - Time zones and windows.
  - Campaign validation and status.
  - Illegal transitions.
  - The live happy path.
  - Unverified rehearsal and unverified submit.
  - Claims, company cooldown and duplicate postings.
  - Writer skip and unavailable stages.
  - Backoff and the email route.
  - Crash at six points (writing, rehearsal fill, live fill, after the employer received it, mid-email, after the outcome was journaled), plus "already sent elsewhere": a second engine on the same database never submits twice.
  - Pacing over 36 h on a `FakeClock` driven through the engine's own timer loop: only inside 09:00–18:00 Karachi, gaps within 10–20 min, 4 a day, keep-awake held inside hours and released outside.
  - Dry run → live: 2 rehearsal days, live on day 3, rehearsed roles re-sent, packets reused, digest says so.
  - Auto-end with a final digest.
  - Kill: running fill stopped in under 5 s, live kill goes to needs_you, a fill that ignores the abort, the STOP file, monthly and campaign budgets, a BUDGET error from the writer.
  - Answered question re-queues the job.
  - A fixture-day digest.
  - Telegram: parsing, chat-id lock, every command against a real engine, questions and answers, the poller, fan-out with a dead channel, the offline guard.
  - Keep-awake.
  - Routes.
  - The hunt shim.
- `npm run typecheck` and the full `npm run selfcheck` (162 checks) pass.
- Manual run: I started the server with `BUREAU_PORT=47391 BUREAU_DATA_DIR=<temp> BUREAU_NOTIFY_OFFLINE=1` and drove it over HTTP with a session and CSRF:
  - Create and start a campaign, read status, `/api/hunt`, `/api/notify`, kill, clear kill, end with a final digest, list digests.
  - The other modules' stubs were logged as unavailable, not fatal.
  - The PowerShell keep-awake helper was observed running while a campaign was in its hours, and gone after pause.
- To use Telegram: create a bot with @BotFather, then `PUT /api/notify/telegram {token}`. Message the bot, read your chat id from `GET /api/notify/telegram/chats`, `PUT /api/notify/telegram {chatId}`, then `POST /api/notify/test {channel:'telegram'}`.
- Kill from a shell: create `data/STOP` (under `BUREAU_DATA_DIR`). Delete it, then resume a campaign to continue.

## Acceptance

- ✅ **Start a campaign, kill the process mid-fill, restart: it resumes with no duplicates.** Proven in selfcheck at six crash points, including "the employer already got it". A live fill interrupted mid-way goes to needs_you rather than risking a second submit. Not yet run against a real form; A05 is still a stub here.
- ✅ **Dry-run days switch to live automatically on schedule.** Day boundaries are in the campaign's time zone. At the switch, rehearsed roles are re-queued, an info notification goes out and the digest says "live since today". Proven on a fake clock.
- ❌ **Telegram alerts, digest, questions and commands all work (verified with a test bot).** All of it is built and verified against a mocked Bot API: the chat-id lock, every command, questions out and answers back, alerts, digest and the poller offset. It was **not** verified with a real test bot, because the rules for this build forbid sending real Telegram messages during development. A one-minute check with a real bot (steps above) is a follow-up for the owner or lead.
- ✅ **The campaign auto-ends at `ends_at` with a final digest.**

## Known limits

- Upstream stages are stubs in this worktree: scout (A01), profile sync and the answer bank (A03), writer (A04), form engine (A05), inbox and gap report (A09). Until they land the autopilot logs each one once as unavailable and carries on. In practice nothing gets applied to yet: jobs wait at `selected` (no writer) or `written` (no form engine).
- Campaign budget counts all AI spend since the campaign started, not spend by that campaign (requests §5).
- The browser is closed through the abort signal and `onKill` hooks, which A05 has to honour (requests §3). If a fill ignores the abort, `killAll` still returns within 5 s and pauses everything. The job keeps its submit intent, so recovery decides its fate safely.
- Global daily cap days are the server's local days. Campaign caps use each campaign's own zone.
- The employer time zone comes from a keyword table on the location text. Unknown places are treated as neutral.
- For overnight active windows the daily digest goes out when the window closes and covers that local day so far.
- Unknown questions reach the owner's phone only through Telegram (and the digest). ntfy carries alerts and digests, not questions.
